# restore_deleted_sources misses deletions a PATH-scoped walk would find

## Corrected diagnosis (the original filing was wrong)
This bug was filed claiming plain `git log` skips MERGE commits, so a deletion reaching HEAD
through a merge was invisible. That is FALSE. Measured on the live store against ticket f130's
lost EDIT (a440f6d5-6aa1-4669-9908-5fb955ad6a53, which carried that ticket's 2719-char
description):

    git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/                          -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D --full-history -- <tid>/           -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D -m -- <tid>/                       -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D --diff-merges=first-parent -- ...  -> 0 hits
    git log --all --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/                    -> 0 hits
    git log --all --diff-filter=D        (no pathspec)         -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/*<uuid>*                  -> 1 hit

Every merge-diff mode and `--all` changes nothing. ONLY narrowing the pathspec from the
DIRECTORY to the FILE (or a per-uuid glob) finds it. So this is a pathspec-SCOPE effect under
git's path history simplification — not merge-diff display, and not reachability. The fix the
original acceptance criteria implied (add a diff-merges mode) would have shipped without
fixing anything.

## Impact
`restore_deleted_sources` enumerates deletions with ONE ticket-scoped
`git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- <tid>/` pass. Anything that walk misses stays
unrecoverable and the ticket keeps a SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES finding permanently. Observed on
f130 during the b636 remediation; recovered by hand at the time.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A targeted per-uuid fallback (`git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/*<uuid>*`) recovers
      sources the directory-scoped walk misses.
- [x] The fallback is BOUNDED to the uuids the snapshot still cites as absent after the cheap
      pass — a glob pathspec walks full history per uuid and is markedly slower (one probe
      command timed out at 10 minutes).
- [x] NEWEST-deletion-wins is preserved in the fallback (git streams newest-first, first hit
      wins), matching `_deleted_history`.
- [x] Held-out test: the fallback recovers an event when the directory-scoped walk is stubbed
      empty. Verified RED (fails with the fallback call removed) then GREEN.
- [x] Module-size: `fsck_repair` was at its 800-line cap, so the restore cluster
      (`_deleted_history`, `_deleted_path_for_uuid`, `_uuid_fallback`,
      `restore_deleted_sources`, `rebuild_with_restore`) moves to a new `fsck_restore` leaf —
      633/204 lines, both inside the 100-800 band. `fsck_repair` owns snapshot-source
      ACCOUNTING and the repair decision; `fsck_restore` owns recovering the bytes.
      `fsck_repair` re-exports the public names; `fsck_restore` imports
      `snapshot_missing_sources` lazily so the two do not form a cycle. Neither moved function
      carries a complexity-baseline entry, so the split adds none.
